elements.name: question46
elements.html:
Protocol: PRA-216-301 (Atopic Dermatitis)

Phase: 2a

 

Opening

Thank you for your interest in our clinical trials for atopic dermatitis. As you may know, atopic dermatitis, or eczema is a chronic and often relapsing inflammatory skin diseases that lead to dry, scaly and itchy lesions. Depending on its severity, this can cause major psychological problems, significant sleep loss and a reduced quality of life. As such, Prana Therapeutics is assessing the safety a potential new treatment for atopic dermatitis.

elements.name: question45
elements.html:
Study Drug and Design

This study drug is called ‘PRA-216’, and has been designed to target both what triggers inflammation as well as the inflammation itself. This drug will be administered as a subcutaneous injection into *INJECTION SITE* (either in the abdomen, thigh or shoulder), and there is also a chance of receiving a placebo. You will receive up to 4 doses.

 

As the study is double blinded, neither you not the study team will know which group you’re in until the end of the trial.

 

This study also includes optional photography. Participants may be asked to wear briefs and a bralette while full-body photographs are taken (excluding the face) to assess skin involvement.
 
Participation in the full-body photography component is entirely optional.
 
Participants may choose to:
  • Consent to full-body photography,
  • Consent to photographs of target lesions only, or
  • Decline all study-related photography.

 

No photographs will be taken at the screening visit. If participants choose to participate in the photography component, photographs will be taken at four scheduled time points throughout the study.

elements.name: question47
elements.html:
Study Duration

This study is expected to last around 6 months, with 13 in-clinic visits to the site in Camberwell, segmented between a screening period, dosing period and follow-up period.

 

  • Screening: Day -28 to Day -1
  • Dosing Period: Day 1, 15 and 29 (induction) and Day 85
  • Follow up: Day 86 to Day 197

 

As mentioned, you will receive 4 doses across visits 2, 4, 5 and 7.

 

Your initial screening visit will include another eligibility check from the doctors, including a series of skin examinations and blood testing. Participants should allow up to 4 hours for this visit. 

 

Each dosing visit will also include post-dose monitoring, which can total the visit duration to up to 3 hours.

 

For every other follow-up visit, participants can expect a duration of up to 2 hours.

elements.name: question49
elements.html:
Reimbursement

You will be reimbursed the following for any reasonable travel, parking, meals, and other expenses associated with your study visits.

 

For this study, you will be reimbursed $250 for each in-clinic visit. 

 

As mentioned, there are 13 visits associated with this study, so participants can earn up to $3,250 if they attend each scheduled visit.

 

If you need to return for a repeat blood test, you will be reimbursed $105 for this.

 

In the event that you require an unscheduled visit, you will be reimbursed $250 for each of those.

elements.name: question60
elements.html:
Disclosure

 

Before we go any further, I want to explain exactly how the reimbursement works, so there are no surprises for you later. The reimbursement I just went through is what you'd receive if everything goes ahead as planned. That can look a bit different depending on what happens on the day. For example, if the doctor looks over your information early on and finds you're not eligible before we even get to the consent form, if you decide not to sign the consent form yourself, or if something doesn't line up with what you've told me today, you'd likely only get a partial amount, or in some cases nothing, instead of the full reimbursement.

 

That's actually a big part of why it matters that you're as accurate as possible with me right now. The doctor's early review is based on exactly what you tell me today, so the more accurate you are, the better your chances of making it all the way through screening and getting the full reimbursement.

elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: question43
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
